text: computer multiple cores can apply pixel-wise operations parallel using hsi_tiled(). Workers managed {mirai}. Caution Tiled processing produces reliable results operations work single-pixel basis. Spatial operations median filter must never run way, tiles share border information.

title: Calculate hyperspectral reflectance — hsi_calc_reflectance
text: inputs must share spatial resolution, number bands, wavelength labels, compatible spatial extents. reading .raw ESRI data, load terra::rast(x, noflip = TRUE). Three calibration paths supported: Single session (darkspec = NULL, tint = c(1, 1)): specimen, white reference, dark reference share integration time. scaling needed. simplest workflow produces correct reflectance, though signal--noise lower dual-exposure strategy. Matched darks (darkspec provided): dual-exposure workflow specimen overexposed relative white reference maximise signal. subtraction uses dark reference captured matching integration time. recommended approach dual-exposure scanning. Many scanners capture dark reference per session, matched darks typically available standard workflows. $$R(\lambda) = \frac{specimen - dark_{specimen}}{white - dark_{white}}   \times \frac{t_{white}}{t_{specimen}}$$ Scaled dark (darkspec = NULL, tint values differ): fallback dual-exposure workflows white-session dark reference available. dark reference scaled integration time ratio numerator subtraction. assumes dark current scales linearly integration time. practice, detectors large fixed-pattern noise component scale exposure time. Scaling overestimates specimen dark current, producing severely degraded reflectance — often negative across entire spectra. Use last resort. $$R(\lambda) = \frac{specimen - dark_{white} \times   \frac{t_{specimen}}{t_{white}}}{white - dark_{white}} \times   \frac{t_{white}}{t_{specimen}}$$
